A.question: Does the 2025 British Commons opportunity clustering persist in a distinct later calendar window, Jan–Sep 2026, without selecting on the 2026 outcome?
A.outcome: division counts from published division IDs
A.estimand: weekly dispersion index and fraction in most active quarter of observed weeks
A.interference: bills and legislative calendars cluster votes

B.H1: Dispersion >2 and top-quartile share >0.45 on later 2026 sample
B.H2: Source duplication/corrected dates inflate apparent concentration
B.H0: The 2025 pattern does not meet both thresholds

C.source: mySociety voting-data monthly 2026-01..09, pinned GitHub commit before download
C.controls: Reproduce same calculation on already observed 2025 Jan-Sep months with proper calendar date filtering and deduplication; compare absolute shifts, not p-values
C.falsifier: dispersion <=2 or top quartile share <=0.45; inconsistency with source month checks
C.limitations: Post hoc campaign selection after 2025; not a preregistration from 2025 or an independent issuer, hence not external replication.

D.QA: Source monthly sha per file; dedupe exact IDs and dates, all tallies nonnegative, no politicians' names stored
D.rights: CC BY 4.0 intermediary plus OPL v3.0 original; do not reuse personal data
